title: University of Oxford Entangles Multi-Species Atom Network and Extends Memory Storage Beyond 10 Seconds
key_facts: University of Oxford physicists published a study in Physical Review Letters (Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160801), 'Multipartite Mixed-Species Entanglement over a Quantum Network'.
They built a heterogeneous quantum network across separate trapped-ion modules using two atomic elements: strontium (88Sr+) and calcium (43Ca+).

They generated entangled (GHZ) states of up to 4 qubits across macroscopic distances and stored the distributed entanglement in calcium memory qubits for more than 10 seconds, extending entanglement lifetimes by more than 100x over the creation time.

Using one species for both networking and storage is a trade-off, because the laser pulses and photon emissions needed for networking disturb nearby memory qubits; the team uses a strontium ion as the network interface and a calcium ion as the memory at each node.
Photons emitted at 422 nm from the strontium ions interfere at a central station to create remote entanglement, which local 402 nm laser pulses then transfer onto the calcium memory qubits.
The calcium memory preserved remote entanglement for more than 10 seconds (reported time constant 14 +/- 4 s), against an average entanglement generation time of about 100 ms.
Quantum Computing Report says this clears a major hurdle for distributed quantum computing and quantum sensing networks.
quote_evidence: In a study published in Physical Review Letters, physicists at the University of Oxford have demonstrated a heterogeneous quantum network that generates multipartite entangled states across separate trapped-ion modules using two distinct atomic elements: strontium (88Sr+) and calcium (43Ca+).
exceeding the average entanglement generation time (~100 ms) by two orders of magnitude and clearing a major hurdle for distributed quantum computing and quantum sensing networks.
why_it_matters_hint: Holding entanglement between distant modules for over 10 seconds is the kind of storage a network of quantum computers or sensors would need.
event_date: Paper publication date not stated; trade-site report 17 Oct 2026
